members.name: persuasion_v4
members.instructions: {"task": "In a charity-donation chat, a persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate to Save the Children. Tag ONLY the final 'Persuader message to tag' with the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses. Use the earlier chat only as context (e.g. to tell an answer from a statement). Note the context lines may be out of order.", "rules": ["Statements about the organisation itself default to credibility, even when answering a question.", "Pick logical over credibility only when the message centres on what the donation will achieve; pick emotion when it foregrounds children's suffering.", "Short replies: genuine agreement/reaction is acknowledgement; flat fillers, bare yes/no answers, confirmations and closings without thanks are other.", "Off-task is very rare; chit-chat usually is greeting, an inquiry, acknowledgement or other."]}

criteria.greeting: Opening social greeting: 'Hi!', 'Hello there', 'Hi, how are you today?', 'How are you?', introducing oneself at the start of the chat; also the persuader's reply to a 'how are you?' in the opening small talk: 'Not bad.', 'Doing alright..', 'I'm good, how are you?', 'I am doing well thank you.'
criteria.personal_inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life or past experiences relevant to giving: 'Do you have children?', 'Have you ever donated to a charity before?', 'Do you usually donate to charities?', 'Where are you from?'.
criteria.task_inquiry: Asks the persuadee's opinion, feelings, knowledge or expectations about the topic/task (children's welfare, charity, the cause), e.g. 'Is this something you care about?', 'Are you interested?', 'What do you think about children in war zones?', 'Have you heard about children separated at the border?', 'Is there any information I could provide?', suggestions phrased as questions such as 'Or how about an office pool to raise money?', 'Could you ask your friends to help?'.
criteria.source_inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows or has heard of the organisation Save the Children: 'Have you heard of Save the Children?', 'Are you familiar with the organization?', 'What do you know about Save the Children?'.
criteria.credibility: Any statement about Save the Children itself: what it is, its programs, where it works, its history, founder, ratings, reputation, trustworthiness, how much of the money reaches children, partnerships, celebrity links, its website; also answers to the persuadee's questions about the charity. Default for statements about the organisation.
criteria.url: A message that is just a website link / 'URL', or points the persuadee to the charity's website.
criteria.logical: Reasoning about what a donation will achieve or why giving makes sense: 'Your donation could help many young children', 'Donations make a huge difference in these kids' lives', 'they can only help when people donate', 'we can work to make up the small amount', 'You can protect those children if you donate! YOU can make a difference'. Centred on the effect of donating, not on describing the charity.
criteria.emotion: Foregrounds children's suffering or tries to stir feelings (sadness, guilt, empathy, hope): statistics of children dying or killed, vivid descriptions of hardship, 'It makes me so sad...', 'imagine a child...', guilt-tripping the persuadee.
criteria.foot_in_door: Argues that even a small amount helps or starts with a small request: 'Every little bit helps', 'Any amount is welcome', 'Even 10 cents would make a difference', 'Half of 1 dollar?', '$2 you won't miss'.
criteria.self_modeling: The persuader states their own donation or intention to donate, as a role model: 'I will donate too', 'I'll match your donation', 'I gave what was given to me', 'I usually donate to this cause yearly', answers about the persuader's own giving.
criteria.personal_story: The persuader tells a narrative or anecdote from their own life or someone's story: 'I worked in Africa earlier this year and saw...', a story about a specific child or family.
criteria.donation_info: Explains how the donation works: it is deducted from the task payment, can be from $0 to $2, the research team collects and sends it to Save the Children, how to pay.
criteria.proposition: A request for the persuadee themself to donate (no specific amount), even with a short reason attached: 'Would you be willing to donate some of your payment?', 'Would you donate then?', 'Hello, would you please donate to help save the children?', 'We are asking people to give part of their payment to the charity', 'Would you consider donating to them?'. NOT a statement of what a donation would achieve ('YOU can protect those children if you donate, you can make a difference' is logical), and NOT ideas for raising money from other people ('how about an office pool?' is task inquiry).
criteria.ask_amount: Asks how much the persuadee would donate or suggests a particular amount: 'How much would you like to give?', 'What amount would you feel comfortable donating?', 'May I suggest $.50 or $1?'.
criteria.praise: Compliments or praises the persuadee: 'That's awesome and generous!', 'People like you make the world better', 'you are a very kind person', 'I'm glad you're so willing to help'.
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee, including a closing that contains thanks: 'Thank you so much for your kindness and have a great day.'
criteria.acknowledgement: Genuine agreement with or reaction to what the persuadee just said: 'I agree 100%', 'That's great to hear', 'this is true', 'I understand', 'Me too', 'That horrifies me!', 'North Carolina is nice, I have been there'.
criteria.off_task: Rare: chatter clearly unrelated to the charity, the donation or the persuadee (e.g. a long tangent about something else entirely).
criteria.other_answer: A bare yes/no or short answer to the persuadee's question that is not about the charity or the persuader's giving: 'Yes.', 'Absolutely.', 'Indeed.', 'Yes there are.' (but a reply to 'how are you?' is greeting).
criteria.other_filler: Flat filler or fragment with no strategy: 'Ok...', 'Fine...', 'yeah..', 'yes, indeed.', 'I know what you mean', 'Save the Children is.', 'sorry, I meant'.
criteria.other_confirm: Confirms or repeats the agreed donation amount, or asks the persuadee to confirm it: 'Alright, just to be sure you want to donate 1 dollar?', 'Alright, 20 cents out of the whole task payment.'
criteria.other_closing: A closing without thanks: 'Have a great night!', 'I hope you enjoy the rest of your day.', 'Good luck'.
criteria.other_hit: Remarks about the HIT, MTurk or the number of turns needed: 'we need 10 chats each to complete this hit'.
criteria.other_misc: Anything else that fits none of the strategies or dialogue acts above.

members.name: persuasion_v4b
members.instructions: You are annotating persuasion dialogues where a persuader asks someone to give to the charity Save the Children. Read the conversation for context (its lines may be shuffled), then decide which strategy or dialogue act the LAST message, labelled 'Persuader message to tag', performs. Facts about the charity itself count as credibility by default, also when they answer a question; choose logical only if the message is about what the donor's money will accomplish, and emotion if it dwells on children's suffering. Real agreement or reaction is acknowledgement, while empty fillers, bare yes/no replies, amount confirmations and goodbyes without thanks are other. Off-task is almost never used.
